name: Tramadol
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Severe persistent pain needing an opioid (extended-release capsules; opioid-naive or converting from other opioids)
usual_adult_dose.dose: 100 mg once daily; titrate by 100 mg every 5 days as needed; maximum 300 mg/day. From tramadol IR: start at the 24-hour IR total rounded down to the next 100 mg

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Benzodiazepines and other CNS depressants (incl. gabapentin, pregabalin, other opioids, alcohol)
key_interactions.effect: Hypotension, profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, death.
key_interactions.action: Reserve for patients without alternatives; use the lowest doses and shortest duration; monitor closely.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, triptans, others)
key_interactions.action: Evaluate often, especially when starting or changing doses; stop tramadol if serotonin syndrome is suspected.
Avoid use (within 14 days of an MAOI).

key_interactions.effect: More tramadol, less M1: seizures, serotonin syndrome, or withdrawal; toxicity when the inhibitor stops.
key_interactions.action: Evaluate often; consider lowering tramadol when the inhibitor is stopped.

key_interactions.effect: Higher tramadol and M1 levels; seizures, serotonin syndrome, respiratory depression.
key_interactions.action: Consider lowering the tramadol dose; monitor closely.
Monitor for digoxin toxicity; adjust digoxin.

key_interactions.effect: Altered warfarin effect, raised prothrombin time (postmarketing).

common: Nausea, constipation, dry mouth, somnolence, dizziness, vomiting (≥10% and twice placebo)
serious: Ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolism risk in children (boxed warning)

contraindications: Postoperative use after tonsillectomy and/or adenoidectomy in children younger than 18 years
Acute or severe bronchial asthma in an unmonitored setting
Known or suspected gastrointestinal obstruction including paralytic ileus
Concurrent MAO inhibitor or use within the last 14 days
monitoring: Respiratory status and sedation, especially when starting or increasing the dose
Signs of serotonin syndrome and seizures
Kidney function: do not use the extended-release form at CrCl <30 mL/min

pk.half_life: About 10 hours (tramadol) and 11 hours (M1) with the extended-release capsule
pk.half_life_eskd: Not studied in severe impairment (CrCl <30); M1 exposure 20% to 40% higher at CrCl 30 to 80 (label)
pk.metabolism: Hepatic: N-demethylation (CYP3A4, CYP2B6), O-demethylation to M1 (CYP2D6), conjugation
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 30% unchanged in urine; 60% as metabolites
pk.dialyzability: No: less than 7% of tramadol and M1 removed in a 4-hour dialysis (label).
